https://www.vasp.at/wiki/NUPDOWN

NUPDOWN = [positive real]
Default: NUPDOWN = not set

Description: Sets the difference between the number of electrons in the
up and down spin components.

Allows calculations for a specific spin multiplet, i.e. the difference
of the number of electrons in the up and down spin component will be
kept fixed to the specified value. There is a word of caution required:
If NUPDOWN is set in the INCAR file the initial moment for the charge
density should be the same. Otherwise convergence can slow down. When
starting from atomic charge densities (ICHARG=2), VASP will try to do
this automatically by setting MAGMOM to NUPDOWN/NIONS. The user can of
course overwrite this default by specifying a different MAGMOM (which
should still result in the correct total moment). If one initializes the
charge density from the one-electron wavefunctions, the initial moment
is always correct, because VASP "pushes" the required number of
electrons from the down to the up component. Initializing the charge
density from the CHGCAR file (ICHARG=1), however, the initial moment is
usually incorrect!

If no value is set (or NUPDOWN=-1) a full relaxation will be performed.
This is also the default.

Diffraction pattern optimizations (#4684)

* Compute XRD form factors once per element instead of once per atom

Group sites by element before the vectorized structure-factor
computation: the scattering coefficients, atomic number and
Debye-Waller factor depend only on the element, so the atomic form
factor f(s) and DW damping are evaluated per unique element over all
hkl rather than per atom, and the per-element phase sums become
occupancy-weighted (M, m_element) matrix products.

This replaces the (M, N_atoms, n_coeff) broadcast with per-element
(M, n_coeff) work, cutting both time and peak memory for large
low-symmetry cells with few species (MD snapshots). Benchmarks with
CuKa over (0, 90) two-theta: 2.8x on a 756-atom perturbed LiFePO4
3x3x3 P1 cell (1.28 s -> 0.45 s), 1.6x on Li10GeP2S12. Patterns agree
with the previous implementation to machine precision (max relative
intensity difference 5e-16, identical peak positions, d-spacings and
hkl families across CsCl, LiFePO4, Li10GeP2S12, Graphite, a disordered
Cu-Au alloy and the P1 supercell). A side effect is that elements with
different scattering-coefficient row counts no longer share one array,
so ragged coefficient sets now work too.

Add a regression test for the grouping-sensitive path: disordered fcc
Cu-Au with oxidation-state species, partial occupancies and per-element
Debye-Waller factors, with reference values generated by the previous
per-atom implementation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Bound XRD structure-factor memory with chunked accumulation

Accumulate the per-element occupancy-weighted phase sums in chunks of
hkl rows so the (chunk, m) phase matrix exp(2 pi i g.r) never exceeds
PHASE_CHUNK_ENTRIES entries (2^22 complex128 = 64 MB), instead of
materializing the full (M, m) matrix. The full matrix scales as
n_hkl x n_atoms and dominates peak memory for large low-symmetry cells
and wide two-theta ranges, eventually OOMing structures the pre-
vectorization loop could handle.

Peak RSS for get_pattern with CuKa over (0, 90), measured in a fresh
process: LiFePO4 4x4x4 (1792 atoms) 2878 MB -> 432 MB (6.7x), 3x3x3
745 MB -> 448 MB; runtime unchanged (1.90 s -> 1.71 s and 0.42 s ->
0.42 s respectively). Patterns are bit-identical to the unchunked
implementation across the whole validation suite (CsCl, LiFePO4,
Li10GeP2S12, Graphite, disordered Cu-Au, perturbed 756-atom P1 cell):
zero difference in positions, intensities, d-spacings and hkl families.

Add a regression test forcing one hkl row per chunk
(PHASE_CHUNK_ENTRIES = 1) and requiring the same pattern as the
default single-chunk path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Halve XRD reciprocal-space work via Friedel's law

The atomic scattering factors are real (anomalous dispersion is not
modeled), so Friedel's law I(g) = I(-g) holds exactly through
F(-g) = F*(g). Compute only the half-space with (h, k, l)
lexicographically positive, double the intensities, and restore the -g
Miller indices when collecting hkl families, so reported families,
multiplicities, peak positions and d-spacings are unchanged. The
Python sort of reciprocal points is replaced by an equivalent stable
np.lexsort on the kept half, with identical ordering semantics.

Speedup on top of the per-element/chunked implementation (best of

The ferri_by_motif_{symbol}_flip skip for a motif that is exactly half
the magnetic sites assumed the global "afm" constraint (order
parameter 0.5) was always present to make it a duplicate. If a caller

unreachable. Only skip when "antiferromagnetic" is in self.strategies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Build whole-motif flips directly instead of via a global order parameter

ferri_by_motif_{symbol}_flip expressed the flip as a single global order
parameter, num_motif_sites / num_mag_sites. That constrains only how many
spins point up, not which sites carry them, so it enumerated every
arrangement with that count: on Fe3O4 six orderings, of which one is a
whole-motif flip and the rest break a motif internally. The Neel state was
reached only by being the most symmetric of the six, so truncate_by_symmetry
or max_orderings could drop it on another structure.

A whole-motif flip needs no enumeration at all. With every motif internally
FM the magnetic cell is the crystallographic primitive cell, so the choice of
which motifs to flip fixes the ordering outright. _add_whole_motif_flips
builds them directly and appends to ordered_structures, as the fm ordering
already does.

One or more motifs may be flipped: every non-empty subset, 2**(n-1) - 1
orderings. The first motif is held pointing up, so a flip and its global spin
inversion are never both emitted instead of the pair being left to the
duplicate pruning downstream.

Drops the order parameter == 0.5 guard, which skipped a motif spanning half
the magnetic sites because the order parameter duplicated the global afm
constraint. A directly built flip costs no enumeration and is always emitted.

wyckoff_symbols is sorted by descending multiplicity so the origin labels are
reproducible; iterating a set varied with PYTHONHASHSEED.

* Document side effects and output size of whole-motif flips

_generate_transformations appends orderings that need no enumeration
(fm and the whole-motif flips) directly to self.ordered_structures;
say so in its docstring rather than leaving it implied by the return
type.

State in _add_whole_motif_flips that n motifs give 2**(n-1) - 1
orderings, bounded at 127 by max_unique_sites, and that all of them
keep the full crystal symmetry and so survive truncate_by_symmetry.
